correctness.rationale: Odd squarefree four-prime integers are deficient since sigma(n)/n <= 2304/1155 <2. Thus all candidate inputs are n=2pqr, for which D=(3p+3q+3-pq)r+3(p+1)(q+1). Monotonic abundancy bounds leave p in {3,5,7}; partition by r-divisibility of omitted divisors proves q<=23 when p=3 and r<=167 in all cases. The actual standalone checker enumerates all 399 remaining triples and each of their 15 proper divisors, finding exactly fifteen solutions with unique omitted pairs. The global result relies on proved reductions, not a numerical extrapolation.

value.rationale: A complete classification of the natural squarefree four-distinct-prime family (both parity cases), extending the 2023 source motivation and distinct from prior two- and three-prime results.
